title: Latency-aware Cost Fallback Protocol (LACFP) Design Spec
author: Leah Chen
content:
Summary:
This design spec defines the Latency-aware Cost Fallback Protocol (LACFP), a server-side policy and lightweight protocol that enables Redwood inference routing to automatically fall back to lower-cost model variants or capacity tiers when latency, cost, or capacity signals indicate it is appropriate. The goal is to preserve user-facing latency SLOs while minimizing incremental cost and providing transparent accounting for customer billing and internal cost centers.

Motivation:
- Customers require predictable latency for interactive workloads (e.g., chat) but also demand cost efficiency.
- Static fallback rules (time-based or simple capacity thresholds) are brittle and cause noisy behavior during transient events.
- We need a shared, auditable protocol that:
  1) reacts to latency and cost signals in near real-time;
  2) guarantees bounded user-impact by enforcing soft/hard fidelity and latency limits;
  3) preserves billable attribution and enables credits/discounting when lower-fidelity fallbacks are applied.

Design goals (must):
- Latency-first: Respect per-route latency SLOs (default 95th pct <= 120ms for token production in interactive endpoints).
- Cost-conscious: Prefer lower-cost variants when they do not violate quality or latency objectives.
- Transparent accounting: Emit events for every fallback decision with cost delta metadata for billing reconciliation.
- Configurable: Support per-tenant and per-route policies with hierarchical inheritance (global -> tenant -> route).

Non-goals (out of scope):
- Model distillation, model training, or quality-aware model retraining.
- Deep content-aware fidelity negotiation (that belongs to the fidelity negotiator PRD).
- Full rewrites of the billing system; LACFP only emits metadata consumed by billing services.

Assumptions:
- Runtime can measure per-request latency to the active model variant and expose aggregated 1m/5m windows.
- Cost-per-token or cost-per-second estimates are available for each variant and capacity tier.
- Each model variant has a compatibility label set (e.g., conversational-v1, embeddings-v2) so fallbacks only target compatible variants.

High-level protocol overview:
- LACFP runs inside the request routing stack. When a request arrives, router evaluates the active policy for the tenant/route and does the following:
  1) Compute expected latency and cost for the request given current telemetry (historical per-variant latency distribution + queue depth).
  2) Evaluate policy rules (latency budget, cost delta threshold, fallback budget).
  3) If policy triggers, select a fallback variant and attach a Fallback-Decision header to the upstream call; emit a fallback event to telemetry.
  4) Billing and credits: tag request with cost-override metadata and store the decision event for offline reconciliation.

State machine and decision logic (simplified):
- States: Normal, SoftFallbacking, HardFallbacking, Stabilizing.
- Trigger signals: 
  * Latency breach probability > P_soft (default 0.25) over 1m window -> SoftFallbacking.
  * Latency breach probability > P_hard (default 0.6) and queue backlog > Q_hard -> HardFallbacking.
  * Cost spike detection: cost-per-token delta > C_threshold (default +50%) -> consider SoftFallback.
- Stabilization: After a fallback, hold policy for a hold_time (default 30s) and require metric improvement across 2 windows before reverting.

Fallback selection heuristics:
- Preferred order: smaller model variant -> quantized variant -> lower-shape instance -> regional shift (if latency permits) -> graceful truncation (session-level fidelity actions handled by fidelity negotiator).
- Only select variants with Compatibility = true for route.
- Respect tenant affinity: if tenant has reserved Dedicated capacity, avoid fallback to shared-hosted unless policy explicitly allows it.

Cost attribution and crediting rules:
- Every decision emits an event payload with: request_id, route_id, tenant_id, timestamp, active_variant, fallback_variant, estimated_cost_delta, latency_estimate_before, latency_estimate_after, reason_tags.
- For customer-facing billing: If fallback reduces cost by >= 10% and the tenant holds a fidelity-safety guarantee, apply a 'fallback-credit' equal to 50% of the cost savings for that billing window (configurable per contract).
- Internal cost centers receive raw cost delta events for chargeback.

Sample cost accounting table (reference):
| Variant | Token CPI (USD) | Avg latency (ms) | Notes |
| small-7b | 0.0008 | 90 | quantized fast path available |
| base-7b-q4 | 0.0005 | 110 | 4-bit quantized variant |
| midsize-13b | 0.0016 | 140 | higher quality, higher cost |

APIs and configuration examples:
- Policy YAML (per-route):

policy: |
  name: lacfp-small-chat-policy
  scope: route
  latency_slo_ms: 120
  soft_trigger_probability: 0.25
  hard_trigger_probability: 0.6
  cost_delta_threshold_pct: 30
  allowed_fallbacks:
    - variant: base-7b-q4
      max_daily_usage_pct: 40
    - variant: small-7b
      max_daily_usage_pct: 20
  hold_time_seconds: 30
  tenant_override: true

- Runtime header injected when fallback applied (HTTP):
  Fallback-Decision: variant=base-7b-q4;reason=latency-soft;estimated_savings=22.4%;credit_tag=fb-50pct

Sample event JSON emitted to telemetry (flattened for ingestion):
  {"request_id":"req_12345","tenant_id":"t_678","route":"/v1/chat","active_variant":"midsize-13b","fallback_variant":"base-7b-q4","estimated_cost_delta_usd":"0.0012","latency_est_before_ms":"160","latency_est_after_ms":"115","reason":"latency_hazard","policy_id":"lacfp-small-chat-policy"}

Backward compatibility and migration:
- Existing per-route fallback rules will be translated into an initial LACFP policy during rollout.
- If runtime does not support LACFP for a capacity pool, the router falls back to previous behavior and emits a compatibility_warning metric.

Rollout plan (phased):
1) Canary (2 weeks): Enable LACFP in a single EU region for internal tenants only. Metrics: false-positive fallback rate < 1%, customer error rate unchanged.
2) Pilot (4–6 weeks): Enable for small set of opt-in customers (20 tenants) across regions. Introduce billing credit hooks in sandbox.
3) Gradual GA (8–12 weeks): Auto-translate legacy fallbacks, expose UI in Console (policy editor), enable for all hosted routes with safe defaults.
4) GA+: Expose per-tenant SLO-driven monetization options and expand to Dedicated routing when tenant permits.

Rollback criteria:
- Error rate increase > 0.5% absolute for a route after rollout.
- Customer support escalations indicating quality regressions (>= 3 within 24 hours).

Telemetry and SLOs to monitor:
- Primary SLO: 95th percentile request latency for interactive routes (target 120ms).
- Metrics to emit: fallback_decisions_count, fallback_rate_per_route, estimated_cost_savings_total, fallback_false_positive_rate, compatibility_warnings, fallout_customer_errors.
- Dashboards: per-tenant fallback summary, per-region stability heatmap, cost-savings ledger for billing reconciliation.

Testing and QA:
- Unit: Decision engine deterministic tests for stochastic triggers.
- Integration: Synthetic load tests simulating queue-backlog and model latency spikes with traffic replay.
- E2E: Billing integration test that validates credit events are generated and consumed by billing pipeline (sanity check: credit and invoice reconciliation end-to-end).

Security and privacy considerations:
- All fallback events contain only tenant and routing metadata; no prompt or response payloads are included in fallback telemetry.
- Fallback decisions stored for at most 12 months by default; retention configurable per tenant contract.

Ownership and next steps:
- Spec owner: Priya Raman (Product – Runtime Economics).
- Implementation owners: eng-serving-runtime (decision engine) and eng-platform (router + telemetry hooks).
- Short-term milestones (Q1 2027):
  * Prototype decision engine in runtime (Spike) — owner: eng-serving-runtime — due 2027-01-30.
  * Telemetry event schema published and consumed by billing sandbox — owner: eng-platform — due 2027-02-10.
  * Console policy editor wireframes — owner: product-ux — due 2027-02-28.

Appendix A — Example debug CLI commands:
- Force a soft fallback test for tenant: redwoodctl routing simulate-fallback --tenant t_678 --route /v1/chat --variant base-7b-q4 --duration 60s
- Inspect last 100 fallback events: redwoodctl telemetry query --filter "event_type=fallback_decision AND tenant=t_678" --limit 100

Appendix B — Open questions for review:
1) Should fallback credits be proportional to realized-line-item savings or based on estimated savings at decision time? Recommendation: start with estimated savings to allow near-real-time customer transparency, revert to realized reconciliation in billing batch.
2) How strict should compatibility labels be for multi-modal endpoints? Recommendation: conservative by default; expose opt-in to relaxed compatibility.
3) Do we allow cross-tenant fallback into Dedicated pools in crisis scenarios? Strong recommendation: no, unless emergency escalation with explicit owner approval.

Document change log:
